title: Novel AI/ML & Computational Science Methods in Pharmaceutical Workflows

content.abstract_summary: A Claude-generated structured review of novel AI/ML methods in pharmaceutical workflows, explicitly grounded in PubMed literature (searches conducted May 2026, all DOIs linked). Organized into four stages: Literature & Background Research, Model Building (Target ID & Lead Discovery), Implementation (Preclinical to Clinical), and Output (Safety, Monitoring & Post-Market Surveillance). More rigorously sourced than the companion ChatGPT background document.
key_findings: DrugProt (BERT/BioBERT on 5,000+ PubMed abstracts) produced a knowledge graph with ~54M nodes and ~19M edges, with precision/recall 0.92–0.95 for specific chemical-protein relation types
TARGETFLOW (LLM-based mining pipeline): 56% high-potential target validation rate and 100% novel-target validation pass rate on rheumatoid arthritis and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
DrugCLIP (contrastive learning framework, Science 2026): virtual screening up to 10 million times faster than traditional molecular docking, tested on ~10,000 human proteins vs. 500M compounds
MM-TcoCPin GNN: AUC = 0.93, F1 = 0.92 for chemical-protein interaction prediction with ablation-validated multimodal contributions
Clinical trial optimization using persona-driven LLM frameworks: 60–70% timeline reductions reported in a 2025 Drug Discovery Today review
XGBoost + SHAP on FAERS database for pharmacovigilance: AUC = 0.738 for predicting drug-associated miscarriage; SHAP identified adalimumab and infliximab as strongest predictors
Model-informed precision dosing (MIPD) with NeuralODEs and LSTM handles sparse, irregular PK data better than classical compartmental approaches
limitations: Claude-generated synthesis; while grounded in PubMed literature, the framing and selection of which papers to highlight reflects Claude's judgment, not a systematic PRISMA review
Only pages 1-5 of a longer document read — post-market surveillance and manufacturing sections may contain additional relevant findings
Literature cutoff May 2026; does not include publications after that date

extracted_claims.text: "The DrugProt initiative at BioCreative VII demonstrates scalability: deep learning systems built on BERT/BioBERT applied to over 5,000 PubMed abstracts generated a silver-standard knowledge graph with ~54 million nodes and ~19 million edges encoding chemical–protein interactions, with precision and recall values reaching 0.92 and 0.95 for specific relation types."
extracted_claims.location: Section 1: Literature & Background Research — Named Entity Recognition

extracted_claims.text: "A landmark 2026 paper in Science describes DrugCLIP, a contrastive learning framework enabling virtual screening up to 10 million times faster than traditional molecular docking. Tested on ~10,000 human proteins screened against 500 million compounds, it achieved a 15% hit rate against the norepinephrine transporter and a 17.5% hit rate against a target (TRIP12) using only AlphaFold2-predicted structures."
extracted_claims.location: Section 2: Model Building — Contrastive Learning for Genome-Wide Virtual Screening

extracted_claims.text: "A 2025 Drug Discovery Today review documents 60-70% timeline reductions and improved clinical trial efficiency using [persona-driven LLM] approaches, while flagging ongoing challenges in hallucination mitigation and regulatory validation."
extracted_claims.location: Section 3: Implementation — AI in Clinical Trial Optimization
